note: First verdict 2026-11-20 by an independent agent, after the annotation was re-homed to plan/post-release/kernel/spec-xfrm-outer-df-set-dscp.md (which lists this row); no tagged unit changed. RFC 4301 Section 5.1.2.1: "If the packet will immediately enter a domain for which the DSCP value in the outer header is not appropriate, that value MUST be mapped to an appropriate value for the domain". Tested: "that value MUST be mapped". Gap: "to an appropriate value for the domain". Producer: internal/component/ike/dataplane/xfrm_linux.go::xfrmDSCPFlag. Positives: the dscp-map leaf parses copy or 0 to 63 per peer (TestDSCPMapIsConfigurablePerPeer); the engine carries the peer's mapping onto the outbound SA with the inbound kept copy (TestOuterHeaderDSCPReachesTheBackend) and across rekey (TestRekeyKeepsTheOuterHeaderTreatment); XFRM builds DontEncapDSCP for 0 and not for copy (TestXFRMStateCarriesTheOuterDSCP); VPP sends ENCAP_COPY_DSCP or Dscp 46 (TestVPPInstallSACarriesTheOuterDSCP); and on the wire an EF inner datagram leaves with DSCP 46 under copy and 0 under the mapping (TestXFRMOuterHeaderCarriesTheOuterDSCP), which asserts one header per send. Negatives: a value XFRM cannot write is refused at state build, at config verify (TestXFRMSAOptionsSupportedRefusesOuterDSCPItCannotWrite, TestVerifyPeerSAOptionsRefusesWhatTheBackendCannotApply, naming the peer) and at install without a degraded Child SA (TestChildSAOptionRefusalIsNotKeptDegraded). The scoped claim holds: the mapping is applied, never silently replaced. The gap (a fixed 1 to 63 on Linux XFRM, a per-class table) stays unmet and is never counted conformant.
